subject: Clarifying SDK contract exemptions and field triage workflow

Subject: Clarifying SDK contract exemptions and field triage workflow

Team — quick context: Velda Health is asking for a narrow SLA/behavior exemption tied to their SDK integration. They see intermittent stream stalls on long multipart prompts which they surface as latency violations in their contract review. Attached is the formal request from procurement plus a trimmed log file from their PoC run.

Ask: can we confirm whether we have a supported surface (SDK flag, runtime knob, or documented mitigation) that we can safely promise to Velda for their Demo/Prod cutover? Procurement needs language for a one-off carve-out for up to 90 days while we validate a mitigation.

What I need from this thread:
- Runtime triage owner to confirm root cause hypothesis and risk (Logan)
- Field repro steps and quick mitigations (Karthik)
- Product note on whether exceptions are acceptable and how they map to rollout/roadmap (Grace)
- A single-sentence reply I can send back to Procurement by EOD.

Attachments: SLA-exception-request.pdf, velda-streaming-logs-0706.txt

Thanks —
Marissa

Thanks Marissa — I can coordinate the write-up to Procurement once we have the technical confidence level. Quick notes after a skim of the logs:
- The attached velda-streaming-logs-0706.txt shows repeated partial-token stalls at ~60–70s into long responses, often followed by a reconnect and retry.
- Hypothesis A: intermittent client-side backpressure/keepalive behavior in their JavaScript client interacting poorly with our continuous-batching window.
- Hypothesis B: a runtime limit on in-flight K/V cache growth for very long multipart prompts causing a soft abort that the SDK surface currently surfaces as a stall rather than a graceful error.

Logan/Karthik — can one of you own a short repro matrix (browser + node + long prompt), and call out an immediate mitigation we can document (flag on SDK or prescriptive timeout/retry pattern)? If we can give Procurement a mitigation statement + a 90-day monitoring SLA, I think Legal may accept the carve-out.

I'll hold the one-sentence reply draft until we have the mitigation text.

Mina

From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 7 Jul 2026 12:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarifying SDK contract exemptions and field triage workflow

Adding technical detail from a runtime perspective:
- I ran an internal quick-check against a longstanding test harness that reproduces long multipart prompts. We observe the same token-emission pauses when client keepalive falls below 30s and the request stays in the queue while batching logic tries to coalesce payloads.
- This is a behavior at the SDK↔runtime boundary, not strictly model-level. Runtime currently treats prolonged client silence as backpressure; the SDK surface retries but doesn't currently expose a way to force immediate flush / serialize.

Immediate mitigation options (short-term):
1) SDK client-side: expose a "flush_immediately" boolean on the streaming client so the request bypasses batching and is sent as a dedicated window. Low-risk change in SDK surface; quick rollout possible (minor client semver bump).
2) Runtime policy: allow a per-request header (x-redwood-stream-mode: direct) that instructs router to avoid cross-request coalescing for that connection. Requires a conservative rollout and a short-term perf cost.

I recommend we offer (1) to Velda as the documented mitigation and simultaneously log an opt-in runtime header (2) for internal telemetry to quantify impact. Karthik — if you can capture repro steps for browser + node and confirm (1) fixes it locally, we'll be able to give Procurement the language.

—Logan
Logan Wright
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
logan_wright@redwood.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 7 Jul 2026 15:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarifying SDK contract exemptions and field triage workflow

Repro notes and quick test results — I executed a two-step repro and verified Logan's mitigation:
1) Repro steps (browser):
   - Use SDK v1.8.2 (browser bundle), open a streaming session with a multipart prompt ~4–6k tokens total.
   - Simulate intermittent client pause: call send() chunks with 35s gap between two chunks.
   - Observe: token emission pauses ~60s, then connection retries.
2) Repro steps (node):
   - node v18, SDK v1.8.2, same payload; use ncat to simulate network pause. Same pause observed.

Quick fix validation: I added a temporary local toggle in the SDK client (flush_immediately: true) — with the toggle the streaming request is serialized and the pauses disappear in both browser and node runs. No runtime error, just consistent token flow.

Notes for shipping:
- Proposed immediate change: publish SDK flag (flush_immediately) as experimental in v1.8.3; doc the perf implications (higher per-token cost).
- Proposed telemetry: include x-redwood-stream-mode header when flag is used so we can measure load.
- Risk: customers using the flag will see increased per-token cost; we should add a billing note in the docs and a flag gating (beta).

I can prepare a small code snippet and sample test harness; will upload to Drive link and add to the Jira.

Karthik

Summary and proposed reply to Procurement (one sentence + short appendix):

One-sentence reply (for Procurement):

"Redwood will provide a documented, time-limited mitigation for Velda Health: an SDK-level 'flush_immediately' toggle to bypass batching for affected streaming requests, plus an opt-in runtime header for telemetry; Redwood will monitor the behavior for 90 days and provide weekly status reports to Velda during the monitoring window."

Appendix (technical context, for legal):
- Mitigation: SDK toggle (flush_immediately) to force dedicated request path; documented perf and billing implications.
- Telemetry: we will tag requests with x-redwood-stream-mode when used and create a short Jira (SRV-4987) to capture incidents.
- Rollout: SDK experimental flag in v1.8.3; runtime header gated behind a safe rollout for telemetry.
- Owner & cadence: Karthik will run repro verification and publish the test harness; Logan will add the runtime header scaffolding and telemetry; Mina will own weekly status emails to Velda.

Marissa — if that one-liner looks good I will send it to Procurement and copy Sam. Also: Grace, is the proposed path acceptable as a short-term product exception or do you want the language softened/expanded?

Thanks —
